summary: Since autumn 2023, local teenagers have been shifting from gyms to parks and green spaces for outdoor and green exercise. The note covers teen-led fitness meetups, schools moving PE outdoors, the EcoFit app, new public fitness stations, and environmental efforts like plogging. It presents the trend as a lasting, inclusive and sustainable redefinition of fitness.
one_line: Local teens are leading a shift from gyms to outdoor green exercise, combining community, technology, schools and environmental advocacy.
key_facts: Since the autumn equinox of 2023, more teens have been using local parks and outdoor facilities for workouts.
Studies cited in the note say green exercise can reduce stress and increase happiness.
Gym owner Marcus Green said in an October 5, 2023 interview that teens aren't signing up for gym memberships like they used to.
Sixteen-year-old Jessica Lin started the teen-led group 'Fit & Green Teens' on September 15, 2023; its memberships have skyrocketed.
'Fit & Green Teens' holds weekly meetups including yoga in the park, outdoor circuit training and hiking.
A local survey found over 60% of teens prefer meetups with a fitness component.
Starting in late September, several local schools added outdoor activities to their physical education curriculum; Richard Myles of Lincoln High School said students are more engaged.
The 'Run for Green' program kicked off on September 25, 2023, with outdoor running groups promoting environmental awareness and conservation.
Seventeen-year-old Liam Sanchez launched the 'EcoFit' app on September 1, 2023, merging fitness tracking with environmental challenges and badges.
A local initiative to install fitness stations along popular running trails and in community parks was realized on October 10, 2023.
Alice Redfern, who oversees community recreation programs, said the stations let teens do bodyweight exercises and structured workouts outside the gym.
The 'Green Sprint Weekend' on November 11, 2023 drew hundreds of local teens who cleaned up their exercise spaces.
Teens combine workouts with 'plogging', which is jogging while picking up litter.
Efforts are growing to make outdoor fitness programs accessible regardless of socioeconomic status.
